001package io.jstach.rainbowgum.format;
002
003import io.jstach.rainbowgum.annotation.CaseChanging;
004import io.jstach.rainbowgum.annotation.EnumAlias;
005
006/**
007 * Where an event's key values go in a structured event format such as the core
008 * <code>json</code> encoder.
009 */
010@CaseChanging
011public enum KeyValuesPlacement {
012
013        /**
014         * Alongside the event's own fields, the way logfmt and most log aggregators expect
015         * them. A key value named like one of the event's own fields is placed in the nested
016         * object instead, so nothing is dropped, renamed, or written twice. The default.
017         */
018        @EnumAlias({ "true", "default" })
019        MERGED,
020        /**
021         * In a nested object, written even when there are no key values so every event has
022         * the same shape.
023         */
024        NESTED,
025        /**
026         * Key values are left out.
027         */
028        @EnumAlias("false")
029        NONE;
030
031        static KeyValuesPlacement parse(String value) {
032                return switch (value.strip().toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT)) {
033                        case "true", "default" -> MERGED;
034                        case "false" -> NONE;
035                        default ->
036                                io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogProperty.enumValue(KeyValuesPlacement.class, value, "true", "false", "default");
037                };
038        }
039
040}
